Latest news from Uppsala University
Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to researcher at IceCube
Congratulations to Francis Halzen, researcher at the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the University of Wisconsin–Madison, on winning the Nobel Prize in Physics! Halzen is also an honorary doctor at Uppsala University.
IceCube is one of the world’s most advanced observatories for studying neutrinos that reach us from outer space. Researchers at Uppsala University have been involved since the project’s inception and have made significant contributions to the research.

Music, museums and gardens
Music at Uppsala University
In Uppsala, you can enjoy a vibrant music scene, both as an audience member and as a performer. There are choirs and orchestras here covering a wide range of musical genres.
Museums and collections
Visit one of the University’s museums. Why not bring your family? University staff, students and children get in for free.
The University’s botanical gardens
Botany and horticulture, drawing on the legacy of Rudbeck, Linnaeus and Thunberg.
Uppsala University 550 years
In the service of knowledge since 1477.
The European university alliance ENLIGHT
Uppsala University is part of ENLIGHT, a European university alliance comprising ten research-intensive universities. ENLIGHT works together to promote equality, improved quality of life, sustainability and global engagement through higher education.
